final.answer: P-26-2 feeds two items directly: ball valve BV-26-1 and check valve CHV-26-1. Per its datasheet (Flowserve Worcester F51/F52), BV-26-1 has no single maximum allowable pressure — it depends on the pressure class (Class 150 or 300), body material group (1.2 or 2.2) and seat material, with the pressure/temperature chart on page 6 giving the limit; the highest value in that chart is about 51.8 bar (Group 1.2, Class 300, near 0 °C), and soft-seat limits can be lower. CHV-26-1's datasheet (Swagelok check valves) gives a maximum working pressure of 6000 psig (about 413 bar) for CH4/CH8 valves in 316 SS at 10–100 °F, with lower ratings for other series (e.g. 206 bar for the C series, 137 bar for 12C/16C), and the exact end connection may further limit it. Since BV-26-1's maximum possible rating (about 51.8 bar) is far below even CHV-26-1's lowest plausible series rating (about 137–206 bar), BV-26-1 has the lower maximum allowable pressure of the two under any configuration.

There is no single "maximum allowable pressure" for this valve — it depends on which valve variant (ET, EAT or ETR), which body material and which pressure rating (PN class) you have, and the datasheet says the inlet pressure and temperature must always be limited by the applicable ASME pressure/temperature rating [p. 3, p. 32].

What the datasheet gives:

- **Maximum inlet pressures and temperatures** depend on the body type [p. 3]:
  - Cast iron bodies, flanged: consistent with CL125B or CL250B per ASME B16.1
  - Steel and stainless steel bodies, flanged: consistent with CL150, 300 and 600 per ASME B16.34
  - Steel and stainless steel bodies, screwed or welding: consistent with flanged CL600 per ASME B16.34
  - These apply "as listed below, unless limited by maximum pressure drop or material temperature capabilities" [p. 3]

- **Pressure ratings for steel valve body, raised-face** (Table on p. 5) [p. 5]:
  - ET: PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63, PN100
  - EAT: PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63, PN100
  - ETR: PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63, PN100

- **Packing limit**: with ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF packing, the maximum pressure/temperature limit is 1500 psig (104 bar) at 600 °F (316 °C) (Table 2, p. 5) [p. 5]

- **Key rule repeated throughout**: Do not exceed the maximum pressure and temperature for the pressure rating of the body material used, even though the trims shown may have higher capabilities [p. 18, p. 19, p. 26]. Also, no pressure or temperature limits in the bulletin, nor any applicable code limitations, should be exceeded [p. 3–5].

So to find your exact maximum pressure, you need to know your valve's pressure class (e.g. CL150/300/600 or PN16–PN100) and body material, then apply the corresponding ASME/EN rating — the datasheet references those standards rather than listing every pressure/temperature pair in these facts.

- **Steel or stainless-steel body, flanged:** maximum inlet pressure and temperature are consistent with **CL150, CL300, or CL600**, per ASME B16.34. Certain bonnet-bolting choices may require a CL600 assembly to be derated. [p. 3]
- **Steel or stainless-steel body, screwed or welded:** consistent with **flanged CL600**, per ASME B16.34. [p. 3]
- **Cast-iron body, flanged:** consistent with **CL125B or CL250B**, per ASME B16.1. [p. 3]
- **EN raised-face steel-body options:** the datasheet lists ratings **PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63, and PN100** for ET, EAT, and ETR variants. These are rating designations; the facts provided do not state their pressure equivalents in other units. [p. 5]

The datasheet says inlet limits may be further restricted by maximum pressure drop or material temperature capability, and that the body-material pressure/temperature limit must not be exceeded even if the trim has higher capability. [pp. 3, 18–19] I could not find a single numeric maximum pressure in psi or bar for an unspecified valve construction.
